label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.69), depression scores (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.75), and anxiety scores (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.16) are all in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional difficulties. Despite advanced educational attainment, heavy digital engagement does not appear to buffer against psychological distress, and may coincide with social isolation and mood difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Elevated loneliness consistent with perceived social disconnection
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology across PHQ-9 items
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most elevated of the three distress indicators
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional burden
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of multiple psychological stressors in a high-functioning demographic group

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With mean scores near the floor on all three validated scales (UCLA-8, PHQ-9, and GAD-7), these individuals appear to be functioning well psychologically. They are characterized by higher educational attainment and moderate daily screen or internet use of 1–3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.75, well below clinical concern)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.35, near floor)
Moderate and bounded daily usage pattern (1–3 hours)
Represents a relatively sizable subgroup (n = 116) suggesting a stable, replicable profile

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other clusters. With mean scores well below clinical thresholds on all three validated scales (UCLA-8 loneliness: 1.24, PHQ-9 depression: 0.79, GAD-7 anxiety: 0.83), these individuals demonstrate broadly positive psychological well-being. They are predominantly male, hold graduate-level or higher education, and report moderate daily screen or internet use of 1–3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Low loneliness scores suggesting adequate social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean below 1, well under mild threshold)
Low anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean below 1, well under mild threshold)
Moderate and controlled screen/internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment potentially associated with stronger coping resources
tone: Stable, emotionally resilient, and socially connected
